Rune patterns
Boundary effects
LP2-00–55: doublets across words, wraps and stored corrections
nodes.question: How many of the 86 filtered within-page equal-rune pairs cross stored separators, and do published LP2 reviewed-text edits change them?

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 text, 29 alphabet runes and seven separately stored LP2 reviewed-text layers.
scope.procedure: Find overlapping within-page equal-rune pairs after filtering; inspect source characters between the rune positions and compare the same pairs after stored corrections.
scope.parameters: Five exclusive separator classes; headings included; no page-edge pairs; slash and CR/LF treated as soft row wraps for within-token counting.
scope.exclusions: Second complete independent transcription, new glyph corrections, manual scan verification, alternate word-separator interpretations and cipher identification.

nodes.bounds: Five exclusive separator classes; headings included; no page-edge pairs; slash and CR/LF treated as soft row wraps for within-token counting.
nodes.finding: The archived 86 pairs split 60/3/0/22/1 across contiguous, wrap-only, apostrophe/soft-wrap, hyphen and other-separator classes. The seven stored LP2 reviewed layers leave both pair identities and class totals unchanged.

nodes.bounds: LP2-00–55; no page joining; two apostrophe policies; all selected token pairs, including within-page pairs; anagram lengths >=4 and >=5; identical function/context or shared symbol map only for the respective logical implications.

nodes.label: Doublet context
Ciphertext symbols and differences around LP2 doublets
nodes.question: Do doublet symbols or their neighboring ciphertext differences show extra local ordering beyond the observed zero mask and each page difference inventory?

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00--55 ciphertext rune indices and within-page differences; zero positions and each page nonzero-difference multiset retained.
scope.procedure: Measure doublet-symbol collision pairs and before/after difference imbalance, then shuffle only nonzero differences separately within each page while keeping the observed zero mask and first ciphertext rune. In a companion audit, join boundary categories to event positions and compare complete before/after ciphertext-rune distributions under global and within-page boundary-label shuffles.
scope.parameters: 29-rune modulus; 5,000 difference permutations with seed 330122; 10,000 global and within-page boundary-label permutations with seed 33012217; no cross-page transitions.
scope.exclusions: Plaintext recovery, key inference, probability of the 86-event zero mask, independent full image transcription, English context scoring and post-selection significance.

nodes.bounds: 29-rune modulus; 5,000 difference permutations with seed 330122; 10,000 global and within-page boundary-label permutations with seed 33012217; no cross-page transitions.
nodes.finding: There are 123 same-symbol event pairs and a before/after imbalance of 27.786; both sit within their declared conditional ranges. The 29 event-symbol counts span 0 to 7, and 85 nonzero differences are available on each side. The hyphen-versus-within-token whole-label score is 51.321; 6,495/10,000 global and 8,626/10,000 page-stratified conditional shuffles reach at least that score.
nodes.limitations: Conditioning fixes the 86 zero positions and pagewise difference inventories, so these controls cannot explain the low doublet count or test triple rarity. Boundary-label exchangeability is also only a descriptive benchmark; only 40 events can move in the page-stratified control. Metrics respond to earlier observations and do not supply prospective p-values. The input is archived text, not a new image review.

nodes.label: Doublet events: global versus within-page shuffle controls

scope.representation: One zero-based GP index per overlapping within-page doublet, headings included; remove non-runes and concatenate events in page order.
scope.procedure: Compare three source-specified statistics on the 86-event sequence with 20,000 seeded global shuffles and 20,000 within-page shuffles; also score the largest directed bin and largest three circular bins across lags 1–3.
scope.parameters: Seed 33012026; 20,000 draws per control; one-sided greater-or-equal tails; lags 1–3; 29 directed and 15 circular bins; page event multisets held fixed in the conditioned control.
scope.exclusions: Original unpublished event list and code, other transcriptions, unseen page subsets, all unreported model searches, cipher inference and confirmatory significance claims.

nodes.bounds: Seed 33012026; 20,000 draws per control; one-sided greater-or-equal tails; lags 1–3; 29 directed and 15 circular bins; page event multisets held fixed in the conditioned control.
nodes.finding: For the observed lag-one sum 734, 31/20,000 global shuffles and 3,910/20,000 within-page shuffles meet or exceed it. The observed +4 count 10 has 13 and 23 narrow exceedances, but allowing selection of any directed bin at lags 1–3 gives 1,123 and 3,510 exceedances.
nodes.limitations: The reported statistics and bins were selected after looking at data. These two randomizations are conditional reference models, not models of every plausible encryption process; source p-values cannot be exactly recovered without its inputs and implementation.

nodes.label: What separates LP2’s surviving doublets?
nodes.question: Do six source-defined difference, boundary, periodic, clustering, key-switch or skip-next tests distinguish the 86 surviving LP2 doublets?

scope.representation: Source nine-section LP2-00–55 GP29 stream with written-line and page markers, 12,947 within-section adjacent pairs; site page text independently reconstructs all pair positions and marker flags.
scope.procedure: Run unchanged source H and O unittest classes with synthetic controls; preserve source pair/control input ledger; independently rebuild pairs from site raw pages and recompute H L1–L5 plus O C14.
scope.parameters: L1 28 residues, |z|=3.5; L2 line-break 2.5% rule; L3 31 periods×2 clocks and Bonferroni .01/62; L4 nine sections and 500-pair windows; L5 two named key pairs×ideal/literal switches; O fixed repeat .19 and LLR cutoff −10.
scope.exclusions: Other pair-boundary conventions, unspecified or adaptive key switches, other skip rates/plaintext models, decoder outputs, later cipher layers and any mechanism lacking an independently testable output.

nodes.bounds: L1 28 residues, |z|=3.5; L2 line-break 2.5% rule; L3 31 periods×2 clocks and Bonferroni .01/62; L4 nine sections and 500-pair windows; L5 two named key pairs×ideal/literal switches; O fixed repeat .19 and LLR cutoff −10.
nodes.finding: All 16 selected H/O source assertions pass. The independent checker recreates 12,947 within-section pairs and all 86 doublets from site pages, then recalculates all 62 period/clock rows and remaining manuscript summaries. The strongest nonzero-difference z is −2.58, line breaks hold 4/585 repeats, best period p is 0.0355 versus 0.000161 corrected line, and nine-section p is 0.721. Two named key-switch constructions yield at most 10/2,898 repeats on solved text; the specified skip-next model has LP2 LLR −21.34 below its −10 line.
nodes.limitations: The source pairs join pages within nine sections, unlike the site's page-only 12,901-pair count. The H checks test chosen summaries and their declared selection rules, not all historical questions about doublets. H5 extrapolates from two named key pairs on solved text. O C14 assumes a 0.19 repeat parameter and solved-text difference profile. None decrypts LP2 or excludes arbitrary collision avoidance.

nodes.label: Doublet placement

scope.procedure: Recount all 86 doublets; measure sentence-relative positions modulo 2–8; compare the largest chi-square/df score with the same seven-way maximum in 5,000 placements retaining each section's number of events and the punctuation boundaries. scope.parameters: Nine fixed sections, 86 events, seven moduli, random.Random(3301), 5,000 controls; ties counted in the upper tail.
scope.exclusions: Different punctuation or source text, word-relative and section-relative coordinates, moduli outside 2–8, event identities, cipher-specific nulls and plaintext recovery.

source_topics.source_title: Word, row, page and section boundaries

nodes.label: Do doublets fall at particular section positions?
nodes.question: Do the 86 unsolved-text doublets cluster by their section-relative positions modulo two through eight?

scope.representation: All 12,956 rune positions in the nine LP2 unsolved sections; each doublet event is located by the second rune’s zero-based position within its section.
scope.procedure: Recount adjacent equal-rune events, tabulate the second-rune positions modulo 2–8, compute chi-square divided by m−1 against opportunity-weighted expectations, and retain the largest of seven scores. In 5,000 seeded controls, preserve doublet counts per section but sample their eligible positions uniformly; apply the identical seven-way selection. Add a planted mod-seven placement check.
scope.parameters: Nine fixed sections; 86 doublets; moduli 2–8; 5,000 random.Random(3301) controls; one-sided upper tail, ties counted.
scope.exclusions: Sentence-relative residues, alternative section boundaries, doublet identities, runs or clusters of events, other moduli and cipher-specific position laws.

nodes.bounds: Nine fixed sections; 86 doublets; moduli 2–8; 5,000 random.Random(3301) controls; one-sided upper tail, ties counted.
nodes.finding: The strongest manuscript concentration is chi-square/df 1.168 at modulus 2. A best-of-seven control reaches or exceeds it 4,316 times in 5,000 trials; the source section-relative count vectors reproduce exactly.
nodes.limitations: Uniform placement conditional on each section event count is a positional reference, not a cipher model. Event clustering within sections is not preserved. The source sentence-relative counts need a separate punctuation inventory and are not claimed as reproduced.

nodes.question: Do the 86 adjacent repeats collect at block boundaries for sizes five, seven or thirteen, or at any selected periodic offset?

nodes.label: Entropy & equality structure
Does LP2's rune order reveal a generator?
nodes.question: Does a published first-order entropy dip survive a control that matches the manuscript's scarce adjacent repeats?

scope.representation: Pinned source GP29 transcription, 55 concatenated nonempty LP2 text segments, 12,956 runes; includes cross-segment transitions.
scope.procedure: Replay unchanged 40-iid-control source program exactly. Separately, compare empirical order-zero through order-two conditional entropy to 1,000 seeded controls constructed with exactly 86 adjacent repeat transitions.
scope.parameters: 29 symbols, 12,956 runes, source 40 iid controls seed 3301; new matched controls seed 20261023, 1,000 replicates, 86 repeated transitions each.
scope.exclusions: No pagewise or wordwise matching, exact unigram-count conditioning, held-out predictive entropy, PPM, key search, or decryption.

nodes.bounds: 29 symbols, 12,956 runes, source 40 iid controls seed 3301; new matched controls seed 20261023, 1,000 replicates, 86 repeated transitions each.

nodes.limitations: The new controls were chosen after the anomaly and match only total adjacent repeats, not page structure, exact unigram counts, or word boundaries. In-sample high-order empirical entropy is not a held-out entropy-rate estimate; no key or plaintext is identified.

nodes.label: Equality structure of the LP2-53 red passage
nodes.question: Does the 51-rune red passage on LP2-53 have the equality structure of archived decoded GP passages, and does it differ from the same page’s black text?

nodes.bounds: 51 red runes, 2,492 overlapping solved-section windows, 78 overlapping black-page windows, 10,000 seeded red shuffles.
nodes.finding: Red IoC is 0.0298 with 26 distinct runes; 2,492 archived solved-reading windows have minimum IoC 0.0400 and at most 23 unique runes. Red IoC lies within 78 black-text window values on LP2-53. Its zero adjacent repeats also occur in 21.55% of 10,000 red-rune shuffles.

nodes.question: Does LP2-00–55 have an excess of within-page matching trigram pairs compared with independent whole-page fixed-count shuffles?

nodes.label: Deleting one fixed rune type: adjacent-pair census
nodes.question: Does deleting every occurrence of any one of the 29 rune types reduce LP2's within-page adjacent equal-rune count?

scope.representation: Archived LP2-00–55 UTF-8 text and the site 29-rune alphabet; headings included; non-runes removed before within-page adjacent-pair counts.
scope.procedure: For each rune type separately, delete every occurrence while preserving surviving order and page boundaries; recount equal adjacent rune pairs, destroyed pairs, newly bridged pairs, surviving edges and fixed-count shuffle expectation.
scope.parameters: Exactly 29 fixed global deletion rules. No individual position selection, no threshold optimization, no plaintext scoring, no key or subsequent decoder.

nodes.bounds: Exactly 29 fixed global deletion rules. No individual position selection, no threshold optimization, no plaintext scoring, no key or subsequent decoder.
nodes.finding: No complete one-rune-type deletion reduces the 86 original adjacent equal-rune pairs. The resulting counts range from 92 to 109; the exact bridge identity explains each change. Fixed-count shuffle expectations for the retained streams range from 437.08 to 440.80 pairs.

nodes.label: LP2 sections: rune collisions and adjacent repeats

nodes.label: Where could a repeat filter act?

nodes.label: Does the missing-doublet pattern resemble a lag-one filter?

nodes.label: Crib capacity

nodes.label: Which archived Cicada signatures verify?
nodes.question: Do the signed files in the pinned public Cicada corpus verify against the canonical key, and does the older source table describe the same file snapshot?

scope.exclusions: Files outside this pinned revision, unarchived signed messages, authorship beyond the public key, and any LP2 decryption hypothesis.
scope.parameters: 135 committed .asc paths, 2 source-scratch exclusions, 133 cases; canonical key fingerprint 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F; source controls C1-C4. Supplemental 2013 opening comparison: four files, one exact header-line repair, and identical signature packets.
scope.procedure: Run the pinned source verifier unchanged in an isolated corpus. Separately submit all 133 exact files to GnuPG under a fresh canonical-key-only home, including armored PGP MESSAGE packets; compare source versus independent verdicts and the two source snapshots by path and bytes.
scope.representation: Every .asc Git blob at pinned revision f08b20b, excluding the source verifier's own two work/ control files; exact raw bytes reconstructed from 89 content-addressed blobs at 133 paths. A 1,459-byte extraction from the separately preserved 2013 JPEG is a supplemental comparator, not a 134th source-scan case.

nodes.bounds: 135 committed .asc paths, 2 source-scratch exclusions, 133 cases; canonical key fingerprint 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F; source controls C1-C4. Supplemental 2013 opening comparison: four files, one exact header-line repair, and identical signature packets.
nodes.finding: The unchanged source program reports 114 PASS, 11 KEY, 7 NO-SIG and 1 FAIL. An independent GnuPG pass over every file finds 115 PASS, 11 KEY, 6 NO-SIG and 1 FAIL. The sole difference is tcp-server.asc, whose PGP MESSAGE contains a valid embedded signature. The two source-program snapshots agree on all 123 shared paths, with only LF/CRLF byte differences.
nodes.limitations: The pinned Git corpus contains 133 source-visible .asc files; the older table used 228 working-tree files, including 105 paths missing from this commit. The source program's armor-header heuristic misses embedded signatures, so its 114/7 counts are not the corrected GnuPG verdicts. Validity under the specified public key does not prove historical authorship or cover all messages; this is not an LP2 decryption test.

nodes.label: Round 19 RSA key scan: source replay and provenance
nodes.question: Does the source's expanded 23-modulus RSA scan yield a padding match, and are all 23 keys actually Cicada keys?

scope.representation: Three pinned 256-byte grid readings as whole RSA values, two byte orders and source zero-extension alignments.
scope.procedure: Recompute every Round 19 C1 E-01 source row under its named moduli and exponents, test source structural predicates, and derive OpenPGP fingerprints and moduli from pinned armored witnesses.
scope.parameters: 23 named moduli (22 PGP packets plus one 2013 puzzle modulus), three payload readings, source endian/alignment options, three exponents: 738 named settings, 594 valid and 144 s>=n exclusions.
scope.exclusions: Private-key RSA operations, extra modulus witnesses, unknown keys, partial payload blocks, and alternate padding.

nodes.bounds: 23 named moduli (22 PGP packets plus one 2013 puzzle modulus), three payload readings, source endian/alignment options, three exponents: 738 named settings, 594 valid and 144 s>=n exclusions.
nodes.finding: 594 valid public-power settings produced no source-defined PKCS#1 or PSS structure; 144 inputs were invalid. The 22 parsed PGP packets comprise two Cicada packets and 20 keys archived for unrelated reasons.
nodes.limitations: This is a whole-payload public-power replay and key-provenance audit. It does not test RSA private-key decryption, other byte windows, or unknown keys. The 540 evaluated rows under unrelated keys are exploratory, not Cicada-key coverage.
